purpose: Probe whether vendored oneDNN grouped-memory matmul can create and execute Qwen3.6-like signed INT8 grouped matmul primitives on B70.
quality_scope: API and shape smoke only. This does not use real model weights and is not an endpoint quality or speed claim.

rerun.summary: All 8 probe cases passed after oneDNN/JIT cache warmth.

comparison_context.current_route_replay_gemm_components_us: Layer-9 scratch-hook route replay in data/qwen36-quark-int8-moe-routecapture6-layer9-scratch-hook-20260612au.md measured current grouped GEMM components around 89-125 us per GEMM across the same rows=1 route offsets.
comparison_context.interpretation: oneDNN grouped signed INT8 has the required basic dtype/scale shape support, but direct per-token grouped matmul execution is not competitive with the current XPU grouped-GEMM floor for Qwen rows=1 unless primitive reuse, post-op fusion, or command-bundle integration changes the overhead profile.

decision: Do not route the endpoint through oneDNN grouped matmul as two standalone GEMM calls. Keep oneDNN as a candidate backend for route-signature primitive caches, larger fused MoE islands, or command-bundle/layerlet experiments.
next_steps: If continuing oneDNN, build a single-process replay that creates primitives once, reuses them across many route windows, and times execute without recreating memory objects.
Test oneDNN post-op or graph fusion only if it can absorb activation/gather or reduce command boundaries; two isolated oneDNN GEMMs are too slow.
Use the scratch-hook result to deprioritize xpu_fused_moe scratch wiring as an endpoint candidate: it is exact but slower than base xpu_fused_moe.
